headline: US Congress review commission chair says Chinese coast guard patrols east of Taiwan 'highly destabilizing'
dek: Beijing's TAO defends coast guard 'law enforcement patrols' around Pratas as 'safeguarding order'; Taipei forum: US commission chair calls east-of-Taiwan patrols 'highly destabilizing'; Wu rejects Chinese legal claim to eastern waters.
sources: Reuters; JPost; Taiwan NSC (Joseph Wu); US Congress review commission chair
fault_line: Law enforcement or jurisdiction grab — who actually controls the waters around Pratas?

sections.what_happened: Beijing's TAO defends coast guard 'law enforcement patrols' around Pratas as 'safeguarding order'; Taipei forum: US commission chair calls east-of-Taiwan patrols 'highly destabilizing'; Wu rejects Chinese legal claim to eastern waters.
sections.what_verified: Reuters TAO story (freemalaysiatoday relay, timestamped 21-Oct 11:50); JPost Sabina/Pratas piece; consistent with 0800-01 record.
sections.what_disputed: Beijing's 'indisputable sovereignty' claim vs Taipei's rejection — standard opposing positions; no new physical incident beyond the two approaches since Oct 18.
sections.why_matters: Pratas, day two: Beijing calls it law enforcement, Taipei calls it a sovereignty grab — and Washington's man in Taipei calls it destabilizing.
sections.context: Background: South China Sea — UPDATE to 0800-01: Reuters TAO 'safeguarding order' line now widely relayed; NEW quotes (Taipei forum Tuesday, via JPost): US Congress review commission chair says Chinese coast guard patrols east of Taiwan 'highly destabilizing'; Taiwan NSC secretary-general Joseph Wu: China has no legal claim to waters off Taiwan's east coast; two Pratas approaches since Oct 18; first US FONOP in a year (USS Charleston, Sabina Shoal); >100 Chinese ships along first island chain; Liaoning in Western Pacific
